Item 1.05. Material Cybersecurity Incidents.

On October 2, 2024, TechFirm Inc. (the "Company") detected unauthorized access to a portion of its information technology systems. Upon detection, the Company immediately activated its incident response plan and engaged leading cybersecurity forensic experts to assist in containing and investigating the incident.

The investigation has determined that the threat actor gained access to the Company's customer data environment between September 18, 2024 and October 2, 2024. The Company has evidence that the threat actor exfiltrated certain customer data, including names, email addresses, and in some cases, encrypted payment card information for approximately 1.4 million customers.

The Company has determined that this cybersecurity incident is material. The Company has notified appropriate law enforcement authorities and is in the process of notifying affected customers and applicable state and federal regulatory agencies in accordance with applicable law.

The Company has taken steps to contain the incident, including isolating affected systems, rotating access credentials, and implementing additional monitoring. The Company estimates that it will incur costs related to this incident of between $18 million and $32 million, primarily related to remediation, customer notification, credit monitoring services, and legal and regulatory compliance.

This incident may have an adverse effect on the Company's reputation, customer relationships, and financial results. The Company's cyber liability insurance policy provides coverage of up to $25 million per occurrence, subject to a $2 million retention.
